templates.pattern: A vehicle has an initial velocity of [U] m/s and accelerates uniformly at [ACC] m/s² for [T] seconds. Calculate the final velocity of the vehicle in m/s.
templates.explanation:
Using the equation of motion: v = u + at
= [U] + [ACC] × [T]
= [U] + [ACC*T]
= [RESULT] m/s

This equation applies when acceleration is uniform (constant).

templates.pattern: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at [ACC] m/s² for [T] seconds. Calculate the distance travelled by the car in metres.
templates.explanation:
Using s = ut + ½at² with u = 0 (starts from rest):
s = 0 + 0.5 × [ACC] × [T]²
= 0.5 × [ACC] × [T*T]
= [RESULT] m

When starting from rest, initial velocity u = 0 so the ut term disappears.

templates.pattern: An object has an initial velocity of [U] m/s and accelerates uniformly at [ACC] m/s² for [T] seconds. Calculate the total distance travelled in metres.
templates.explanation:
Using s = ut + ½at²:
= [U] × [T] + 0.5 × [ACC] × [T]²
= [U*T] + 0.5 × [ACC] × [T*T]
= [U*T] + [0.5*ACC*T*T]
= [RESULT] m

Both the initial velocity and acceleration contribute to the total distance.

templates.pattern: An object accelerates uniformly from rest. After travelling [S] m its velocity is [V] m/s. Calculate the acceleration of the object in m/s².
templates.explanation:
Using v² = u² + 2as with u = 0:
a = v² ÷ 2s
= [V]² ÷ (2 × [S])
= [V*V] ÷ [2*S]
= [RESULT] m/s²

This equation links velocity, acceleration and distance without needing time.

templates.pattern: A force of [F] N acts on an object for [T] seconds. Calculate the impulse delivered to the object in N·s.
templates.explanation:
Impulse = Force × Time
= [F] × [T]
= [RESULT] N·s

Impulse equals the change in momentum of the object. It is a vector quantity measured in newton-seconds.

templates.pattern: A vehicle of mass [M] kg is travelling at [V] m/s and is brought to rest in [T] seconds by a braking force. Calculate the magnitude of the braking force in newtons.
templates.explanation:
Braking force = change in momentum ÷ time
= (mass × velocity) ÷ time
= ([M] × [V]) ÷ [T]
= [M*V] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] N

This uses the impulse-momentum theorem: F × t = m × v.

templates.pattern: A [M1] kg trolley moving at [U] m/s collides with a stationary [M2] kg trolley. They stick together after the collision. Calculate their combined velocity after the collision in m/s.
templates.explanation:
Using conservation of momentum:
m₁u₁ = (m₁ + m₂)v
v = m₁u₁ ÷ (m₁ + m₂)
= ([M1] × [U]) ÷ ([M1] + [M2])
= [M1*U] ÷ [M1+M2]
= [RESULT] m/s

Total momentum before collision equals total momentum after collision.

templates.pattern: A [M1] kg object moving at [U] m/s collides with a wall and rebounds at [V] m/s in the opposite direction. The collision lasts [T] seconds. Calculate the average force exerted on the object by the wall in newtons.
templates.explanation:
Change in momentum = m × (v − (−u)) = m × (u + v)
= [M1] × ([U] + [V])
= [M1*(U+V)] kg·m/s

Average force = change in momentum ÷ time
= [M1*(U+V)] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] N

Note: the rebound velocity is in the opposite direction so we add the speeds when calculating momentum change.

templates.pattern: A stone of mass [M] kg is dropped from rest from the top of a cliff of height [H] m. Calculate the distance fallen after [T] seconds. (g = 10 m/s², assume no air resistance)
templates.explanation:
Using s = ut + ½gt² with u = 0:
s = 0.5 × 10 × [T]²
= 5 × [T*T]
= [RESULT] m

The stone must not have hit the ground yet — check that the distance is less than the cliff height [H] m.

templates.pattern: An object of mass [M] kg is dropped from a height of [H] m. Calculate the speed of the object just before it hits the ground in m/s. (g = 10 m/s², assume no air resistance)
templates.explanation:
Using v² = u² + 2gh with u = 0:
v = √(2 × 10 × [H])
= √[2*10*H]
= [RESULT] m/s

This applies conservation of energy: all GPE converts to KE just before impact. Mass cancels out so it does not affect the answer.
